claims.text: Removing Co from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi raises the stacking-fault energy of the resulting FeNiCrMn alloy.
The increase in stacking-fault energy is large enough to alter the balance of deformation mechanisms in FeNiCrMn.
Higher stacking-fault energy suppresses deformation twinning at low strain rates and low temperatures in FeNiCrMn.
Higher stacking-fault energy favors smoother dislocation glide and dynamic recovery at higher strain rates and/or temperatures.
The shift from twinning toward dislocation glide and recovery accounts for the maintained strength–ductility balance of FeNiCrMn under dynamic loading.
The tested Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is a single-phase solid solution without secondary phases.
The FeNiCrMn material is produced by conventional solidification.
FeNiCrMn and equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi should be tensile-tested under matched temperature, strain-rate, and processing conditions.
Stacking-fault energy governs the competition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
The favorable strength–ductility combination associated with low stacking-fault energy and TWIP in CoCrNi can be used to motivate an SFE-mediated mechanism.
At elevated temperatures and high strain rates, FeNiCrMn has enhanced dislocation mobility and dynamic recovery.
Dynamic deformation of CoCrFeMnNi has been studied over broad strain-rate ranges, including rates above 10^3 s^-1.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, dynamically loaded FeNiCrMn will exhibit fewer deformation twins and more continuous dislocation slip.
Relative to CoCrFeMnNi, FeNiCrMn will have a similar or improved strength–ductility balance at high strain rates and elevated temperatures.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to single-phase solid-solution conditions without secondary precipitates and below the phase-stability limit.
Failure to observe reduced twinning or another significant deformation-mode shift in FeNiCrMn relative to CoCrFeMnNi would falsify the proposed SFE mechanism.
Degradation rather than maintenance or improvement of the strength–ductility balance would falsify the stated prediction.

contradictions.description: The initial material is described as a conventionally solidified baseline microstructure, whereas the controlled tests specify comparably recrystallized states. It is unclear whether the intended test concerns the as-solidified state or a subsequently recrystallized state.
